name: easyeda-pro-control
description: Safety-gated EasyEDA adapters, disposable symbol-metadata validation and seven engineering skills.

interface.longDescription: Seven skills cover control, schematics, PCB layout, libraries, manufacturing, design review and extensions. The API inventory distinguishes public subsets, native equivalents, blocked implementations and omissions. The current reviewed tuple provides calculations, environment/unit and editor metadata, PCB layer/identity/geometry reads, Component metadata, Pad parameters and component child-pad lists. Polygon paths, complete stacks, resolved rules, reverse ownership and schematic pin mapping remain unverified. A project-local symbol metadata reader observes exact name, description, tags, template reference, version and ticket without geometry loading or cloud-library fallback. That PCB-context read proves neither hidden-editor absence nor a safe rename baseline. A separate project-only preflight compares caller-supplied expected metadata while excluding editor tabs and hidden frames. It also observes bounded UI actor, client, ticket and clock samples. Caller expectations are not provenance; backend actor/clock, permission, startup completion, saved membership and writer authority remain unverified. Ordinary existing-profile launch, retained-owner window observation and one-shot normal closure support disposable project/PCB opening. Baseline validation retains closed SQL evidence, relaunches and opens only the project with fresh source/cache checks and a startup-prefix observation. Its finish actions normally close the retained replacement generation. After proved termination they preserve a final closed raw SQL/native snapshot before releasing captures. Snapshot failure remains distinct from retirement and never permits replay. Offline baseline analysis compares both retained snapshots without reading the original project. Retirement clock reports describe sampled native clocks, not backend actor or timestamp-producer qualification. These baseline actions neither execute the prepared symbol patch nor prove startup completion or writer readiness. Separate disposable validation actions can dispatch one sealed symbol name/description edit and its internally derived inverse, each requiring exact-phase acknowledgements and complete closed SQL plus reopened-content verification. This validation route is not connected-writer-qualified and does not enable normal design writers. A failed disposable opener can request one normal close through its original retained Job without bridge dispatch, keeping quarantine until terminal retirement. Ordinary opening waits for a bounded native startup-prefix event, not full restoration completion. Closure never chooses Save/Discard or forces exit; acknowledgment and retained termination are separate. Opening can migrate storage and automatically Save. Lost handles, ambiguous launch and quarantine retain their restrictions; inspection never replays operations. Historical abandonment qualifies only specific evidence. The older tuple retains separately guarded readers, footprint typed API operations, native controls, checkpoints and recovery. Current schematic-page, symbol and PCB transactions plus eight metadata writers remain blocked pending current lifecycle adaptation, native structure-job completion and complete SQL-effect proof. Compiled topology and affected exports refuse hidden annotation or Save All. Connected validation is operation- and generation-specific. Arbitrary JavaScript, blind retries and unrestricted Save remain refused. The legacy writer is runtime-disabled. Missing installation files select offline-only startup. The historical reviewed tuple is connected-read-admitted; future mismatches fail closed within each capability profile.
defaultPrompt: Validate the EasyEDA bridge without bypassing compatibility gates.
Inspect the admitted EasyEDA project with exact readers and managed evidence.
Apply the requested typed design change and verify it after saving and reopening.
